key_insight: The paper argues that semi-supervised medical image segmentation works better when labeled samples are chosen to represent the data distribution, rather than by random sampling alone.
clinical_relevance: By improving segmentation performance with far fewer annotations, this approach could help reduce labeling burden and accelerate deployment of AI tools for medical imaging.
method: Distribution-Aware Sample Selection uses Vision Foundation Models and a Density-K-Center algorithm to pick representative labeled cases offline.
Memory-guided Copy-Paste (MCP) retrieves semantic priors from memory to align distributions and handle class imbalance.
An easy-to-hard training schedule helps reduce early pseudo-label noise.
evidence_signal: The authors report strong results across six diverse 2D and 3D datasets, with especially notable gains in extremely low-label settings such as 1/16 labeled data.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the foundation model features and the practical overhead of building and maintaining the memory-based alignment module.
paper_title: Beyond Random Sampling: Distribution-Aware Alignment for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
